subject: giraffe
reasoning:
I'm working out how to build a giraffe using the SDK's joint, chain, and part primitives, trying to piece together the likely API signatures from limited knowledge while keeping the approach safe and minimal.

I'll construct parts by computing cylinder placements between two points for limbs and neck segments, and start sketching rough proportions for the giraffe's overall height and torso position.

I'm planning the joint hierarchy next: hips as root, chest/spine parented to hips, a chain of neck joints leading to the head/jaw/ears/ossicones, a short tail chain, and front/rear leg chains with shoulder-knee-fetlock and hip-hock-fetlock naming, making sure every joint name stays unique across the left and right sides.

For the coat pattern, I'm deciding to scatter flattened patch shapes across the body rather than painting textures, deterministically placing scaled icosahedron patches along the torso, tapered neck, and upper legs by projecting points onto an approximated ellipsoid/cylinder surface and orienting each patch flat against the outward normal.

For the skeleton, I'm attaching patches to their nearest joint bone, building the neck as a series of tapered cylinders between joints tilted along a line, and shaping the head with a scaled sphere skull, a muzzle box, and a separate jaw part anchored to its own joint.

I'm adding eyes, ears, ossicones, a mane of boxes along the neck, and a thin tapered tail with a tuft, plus a rodBetween helper that generates cylinders between two points assuming the geometry's default axis aligns with the bone direction. For the torso I'm scaling a sphere into an ellipsoid centered on the spine bone.

Now I'm planning the chest and hip spheres connected by a box, setting hoof placement so feet sit flush at ground level, and defining the color palette for the coat, patches, belly, and dark features. I'm working out the math for scattering random coat patches across the torso's ellipsoid surface using spherical coordinates to position each patch naturally along the body.

Still writing patch placement logic...

Now I'm defining the joint hierarchy, chaining hips through spine, chest, neck segments, and head with their positions and parent relationships.

Working out leg geometry next: front legs attach near the shoulders and run down through wrist, fetlock, to the ground; rear legs attach at the hips and go through hock and fetlock joints, keeping them fairly straight, with segment radii tapering from thicker upper legs to thinner lower legs and fetlocks.

Now I'm defining the head: a scaled skull sphere, a muzzle box offset forward, a jaw box below it, dark eye spheres set into the sides of the head, flattened ear shapes angled outward and up, and ossicone cylinders positioned on top near the eyes.

I'm also working out the mane geometry, placing small boxes along the back of the neck using perpendicular offsets from the neck's direction vector to position each segment pointing up and back.
